stem: A student plans to find the molar mass of an unknown gas using PV = nRT. The student weighs an evacuated rigid glass flask whose internal volume has been calibrated as 0.5000 L, fills the flask with the gas, measures the absolute pressure of the gas with a pressure sensor attached to the flask, and weighs the filled flask. The gas is dry, and no liquid is present in the flask at any time. Which additional measurement is needed to calculate the molar mass of the gas?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The outside height and diameter of the flask

choices.label: B
choices.text: The vapor pressure of water at room temperature

choices.label: C
choices.text: The temperature of the gas in the flask

choices.label: D
choices.text: The thickness of the flask's glass wall

rationales.A: The outside dimensions only describe the apparatus; the internal volume needed for V is already calibrated, so these dimensions are not needed.
rationales.B: The gas is dry and no water was used, so no water vapor contributes a partial pressure. With only one gas in the flask, P_total = P_gas, and the measured pressure is already the pressure of the gas.
rationales.C: M = mRT/(PV). The mass of gas comes from the two weighings, V is the calibrated 0.5000 L, and P is the measured absolute pressure, so the only missing quantity is T (measured, then converted to kelvins).
rationales.D: The glass thickness only describes the apparatus; the internal volume is already known, so this measurement plays no part in the calculation.

misconception_map.A: Treats a measurement that only identifies the apparatus as necessary
misconception_map.B: Uses total pressure where the partial pressure of the gas is needed
misconception_map.D: Treats a measurement that only identifies the apparatus as necessary
